chapter_title: Concerning the Garment of the Waters: how great is its Measure.
chapter_note: This chapter is dominated by a biographical narrative frame (Mani visiting King Shapur, standing on the Tigris quay during flood). The oldest teaching layer — about the First Man assuming elemental garments, the cosmic rulers consuming vast waters, the binding of the mighty giants, and the eschatological dissolution of the material universe — is embedded within this narrative but extractable. The substrate teaching about the measure of the garment of waters is genuine cosmological-correspondential material about cosmic scale and elemental combat. The Tigris flood serves as a pedagogical occasion that the compilers used to frame this teaching. Gardner's note that the chapter's value lies in 'historical reference' confirms that the narrative frame is the editors' contribution. Paragraph 9 is the purest substrate passage. The chapter lacks the systematic zoomorphic/metal/taste mappings seen in Ch. 6 but preserves cosmic process vocabulary (elements, garments, rulers, binding, dissolution).

paragraphs.temporal_note: Pure narrative frame: references King Shapur (historical proper noun), sets the biographical scene. dialogue_frame score 16.13 confirms formulaic framing. No cosmological content whatsoever.

Extended narrative scene-setting: the Tigris flooding, the month of Pharmouthi, the city being submerged. All register scores are zero — this is purely biographical description establishing the occasion for the teaching. Heavily lacunose but clearly narrative throughout. The specific temporal marker (month of Pharmouthi) and geographical detail (gates of the city, market place) anchor this firmly in the editorial biographical layer.

Narrative scene-setting identifying the participants. institutional=10.2 fires on 'leaders of his church' — institutional vocabulary embedded in the dialogue frame. The phrase identifies Mani's disciples in terms of the organized Manichaean community structure. Primary function remains frame (setting up the dialogue participants), with institutional coloring.

paragraphs.core_text: How great is the power of the garment of the waters? How far shall [it extend]? The source from which all these waters burst forth, how great will it be?
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed dialogue attribution 'One of his disciples then spoke. He says to the apostle:' (frame formula). Removed narrative Tigris description 'That it should enter with the roar of its flood and fill this river Tigris in its vastness like the mighty sea! It has carried waves from river bank to bank, and run from wall to wall.' (specific to narrative scene). Removed 'For they come and come each year at their appointed season!' (observational note about annual flooding, narrative frame).
paragraphs.temporal_note: The substantive cosmological question defines the teaching topic: the power and measure of the garment of the waters, and the nature of the source. 'The garment of the waters' is substrate elemental terminology. The question structure reveals the original teaching outline. The Tigris-specific observations are the editorial frame wrapping the question.

Transitional dialogue attribution: 'Then the apostle says to him' + rhetorical setup ('Why are you astonished... listen to what I am about to tell you'). dialogue_frame=16.0. The phrase 'th[e r]iv[er] that came into being during the first time' is a thin cosmological teaser but functions as transition, not teaching. The paragraph exists entirely to connect the disciple's question to Mani's response.

paragraphs.core_text: [At] the time when the First Man assumed the elements, and stood [fi]rm against the first enmity that had come about in the Darkness, he defied these great and powerful rulers. They are immeasurable, greater than the extent or size of thousands and ten thousands of parasangs. At the start, when he spread the fight against them, he gave them fire and wind; and afterwards he gave the garment of the waters to the rulers of death. So they, the rulers, drank in and consumed those waters. Many [waters] poured forth from the garment of waters [...] the rivers flow. The mouth of the rulers [...] those [...], the warriors of destruction [...] laboured and brought them forth.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed '[the way that I told] you in the Great Gospel' — citation to Mani's own text (institutional/editorial self-reference). This is a 3rd-century editorial act linking the teaching to a specific Manichaean canonical text.
paragraphs.temporal_note: This is the main teaching paragraph. substrate=7.03 confirms cosmological vocabulary. The substrate content describes: (1) the First Man assuming elemental garments, (2) the first enmity in the Darkness, (3) the immeasurable scale of the rulers, (4) the sequential deployment of elements (fire, wind, then water), (5) the rulers consuming the waters. This is cosmic process description — both sides of every mapping stay within the cosmic system. 'Darkness' capitalized as cosmic agent. The citation to 'the Great Gospel' (institutional=3.12) is the only editorial intrusion — a self-referential link typical of the Manichaean editorial layer.

paragraphs.core_text: There were seven (rivers) flowing in to the mouth of each one of them, as they shall not [...] to a single stomach, to their fill; because in turn the descent to its stomach shall burn them with its fire and heat. Those rulers were like the [...] of [...]; they were not emptied; rain and [...] their existent days.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed 'like the great river Tigris [that you] see' — narrative frame comparison anchoring the cosmic teaching to the specific biographical scene at the Tigris quayside.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Substrate teaching about the cosmic rulers consuming the seven rivers: the body-process description (mouth, stomach, fire/heat in the descent) is correspondential — mapping cosmic consumption through bodily metaphor. Both sides stay within the cosmic system. The Tigris comparison ('like the great river Tigris [that you] see') bridges to the narrative frame and was likely added when this teaching was embedded in the biographical episode. Heavily lacunose in the final clauses.

paragraphs.core_text: The measure of that river was expanded seven times, as they flow [...] of the body of the [...] waters [...] now.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed 'The apostle speaks to that elect one:' (dialogue frame attribution). Removed 'Marvel at [...] as you say: Grea[t is] its [...] indeed prolonged, for a bearer [...] but [...] you marvel at this. Marvel first [...] that [...] is the first [...] which came into being i[n] this [...].' (exhortatory framing and heavily lacunose fragments where classification is uncertain).
paragraphs.temporal_note: Very heavily damaged paragraph. dialogue_frame=5.97, institutional=2.99. The dialogue attribution and 'Marvel at' exhortation are clearly later framing. The teaching fragment about the sevenfold measure of the river is substrate (cosmic scale measurement). 'That elect one' is institutional vocabulary (Manichaean ecclesiastical term). The heavy lacunae make confident extraction difficult — I have extracted only the clearly identifiable teaching fragment.

paragraphs.core_text: [...] is how great a struggle, since it has [...] these creatures of destruction, the mighty giants. Behold, they are entwined, bound, and [...] in every place. They are hidden, not revealed before the eyes of every flesh that exists on the land of death [...]. These rulers [...] revealed. The entire universe of flesh will be destroyed and dissolved [...]; all pass away [...]. They will be destroyed with their angry voice, which is mightier than the thunder.
paragraphs.temporal_note: The purest substrate passage in the chapter. substrate=5.06, all other scores zero. Describes cosmic processes impersonally: (1) the binding of the creatures of destruction / mighty giants, (2) their concealment from material beings, (3) the eschatological dissolution of the material universe, (4) destruction by a voice mightier than thunder. Every mapping stays within the cosmic system: 'land of death' is cosmic designation for the material world, 'every flesh' is a cosmic category, 'their angry voice mightier than thunder' is correspondential description. 'Behold' is a pedagogical presentation marker found in ancient teaching voice. No editorial intrusions detected.

paragraphs.core_text: this small stream is reckoned [...] before the vastness of these waters. For only one river from thousands of rivers of water, from the secrets that are not revealed, is the river Tigris upon the earth.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed 'Now, as' (transitional connective) and 'of which I have recounted to you' (dialogue frame — first-person reference to the teaching act).
paragraphs.temporal_note: This paragraph teaches about cosmic scale through comparison: the Tigris is one river from thousands of cosmic rivers 'from the secrets that are not revealed.' The scale teaching (cosmic waters vastly exceed observable waters) is substrate — it's the answer to the chapter's question about the measure of the garment of waters. 'The secrets that are not revealed' is substrate epistemological vocabulary. The Tigris reference, while anchored to the narrative frame, functions here as the teaching's pedagogical illustration of the correspondence between observable and cosmic waters.

Exhortatory closure: 'See [...] and be amazed', 'Marvel at', 'understand how great' — imperative voice directing the audience to wonder. References substrate concepts (measure of the elements of waters, stature of the Man who bore them, the First Man assuming the garment) but does not teach them — instead points back to the preceding teaching with devotional emphasis. The cosmological references serve the exhortation rather than constituting independent teaching. substrate=3.39 fires on the references to First Man and elements but the paragraph's function is exhortation.

Formulaic devotional closure by the disciples: 'We revere you, our master, and we give thanks.' dialogue_frame=15.38. Standard session-closing formula. 'All the greatnesses that are hidden from every person' echoes ¶9's 'hidden, not revealed' and ¶10's 'secrets that are not revealed' — the compilers are tying the frame closure back to the substrate vocabulary, but the function is purely frame/devotional.
